findings.evidence: Non-forced path: `if (!filewatch::changed(g_ptPoll, PtName, GetTickCount(), false, &st)) return;` then `const bool changed = !g_ptPoll.primed || (st != g_ptPoll.last);` followed by `g_ptPoll.last = st; g_ptPoll.primed = true;`. FileWatch.h:77-85 `changed()` already sets `p.last = s; p.primed = true;` before returning true, so by line 1412 `changed` is always false on the non-forced path. The `if (changed) KP_LOG(chPlay, "PLAYTHROUGH %s: ...")` at line 1429 therefore never fires on throttled reloads (including the first load).
findings.suggested_investigation: Compare the value of changed with the stamp returned by filewatch::changed (FileWatch.h:77-85) in a host test: edit levelup_playthroughs.ini while the game runs and check levelup_override_log.txt for a PLAYTHROUGH loaded line. Fix direction for the author: take the changed result from filewatch::changed rather than recomputing it after the poll has already recorded the stamp.
findings.why_it_matters: The 'PLAYTHROUGH loaded/missing' diagnostic that the port was meant to keep is silently lost for every real file change seen by the poll; only forced reloads (ptApply/ptSetPc/ptRemove) log it. Reload behaviour itself is unaffected because rebuildPtCfg runs unconditionally.

findings.evidence: `const char* LogName = "levelup_override_log.txt";` followed by `const bool g_fallbackSet = (KpLog_SetFallbackFile(LogName), true);`, a namespace-scope dynamic initializer that runs when the DLL loads, before KPatchInit (line 97) hands over the API.
